- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x prior high or adjust downward by 1–2% after 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent sentiment > 0.15.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast window (first 5–7 days) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for first 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values or apply 0.5–1.0% dampening factor.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often fails to recognize — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is weak or negative.
